decision_conditions: The proposed development, by virtue of its overall size, scale, mass and design, would result in disproportionate and unsympathetic additions to the property which would fail to appropriately integrate with the existing dwelling or surrounding street scene, creating an overly-enlarged appearance to an otherwise modestly proportioned dwelling. Specifically, the proposed rear extension would subsume the existing rear elevation, failing to appear as appropriately subservient, whilst the proposed right-hand side roof enlargement would overly and inappropriately develop the roof, appearing as an incongruous, unbalanced feature of an unsatisfactory design which detracts from the character and appearance of the dwelling and visual amenity of the surrounding street scene. As such, the proposed development fails to have due regard for Local and National Planning Policy, and would be in direct conflict with Policy BE1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part One - Strategic Policies (2012), Policies D

Insufficient information has been provided to determine whether the development proposed could be constructed without having a detrimental impact upon bats, which are a protected species. The proposal includes comprehensive works to the entire existing roof space, which has reasonable potential to provide suitable roosting for bats. As such, a Preliminary Roost Assessment is required (PRA). Depending on the results of the PRA further bat surveys may be required to confirm the presence/absence of bats, and/or enable a characterisation of the roost, and to inform the appropriate mitigation and enhancement measures. In the absence of this information the impact of the proposed development on protected species cannot be properly understood and it is unclear whether those impacts can be adequately mitigated or compensated against.
